docs.summary:
Tracks which [`SceneTool`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.SceneTool)s are live. There is no exclusive "active tool": every available tool ticks every frame and they coexist, because [`HandleContext`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.HandleContext) already decides which handle owns the cursor. A tool that wants to be modal owns that decision itself - it draws a toggle in the tool strip and returns early while switched off, which is both simpler than an activation state machine and more flexible than one.

Availability is the only gating: a global tool is always available, a component-scoped tool is available while a matching component is selected. [`OnActivated`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.SceneTool~OnActivated) and [`OnDeactivated`](#api~Prowl.Editor.GUI.SceneView.SceneTool~OnDeactivated) fire on those transitions.
Every registered tool, in strip order.

docs.summary: Persistent per-tool settings, one shared instance per type. Stored in [`EditorSettings`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Theming.EditorSettings) rather than project settings because a tool's brush size or grid step is a per-user preference that should follow the user across projects, not something committed alongside the scene.

Drops the settings objects handed out so far, so the next [`Settings<T>`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.RagdollBuilder.Settings) reads them again from [`EditorSettings`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Theming.EditorSettings).
Writes every settings object handed out by [`Settings<T>`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.RagdollBuilder.Settings) into [`EditorSettings`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Theming.EditorSettings), ready for its next save.
